item.text:
Verdict: mixed, leaning no. Putin’s state did deliver some measurable, rule-based improvements in basic services and poverty indicators in 2023, but the gains were narrow and were offset by war-budget crowd-out, inflation, and a political system that kept ordinary people’s prospects dependent on a personalist, repressive order.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Pro | `Additional guarantees for free medical care, social payments for medics, and child benefits` | Government of the Russian Federation | 2023-01-09 | https://government.ru/en/news/47503/ | The government expanded free medical care, rehabilitation, and child benefits, and raised pay/support for some medical workers. This is real service expansion, though it is official self-report and not proof of durable upward mobility. | `6B.10, 6B.2, 6B.5, 6B.7` |
| Pro | `Parents receive children's payments from the Social Fund on a single day of delivery of benefits` | Social Fund of Russia | 2023-01-25 | https://sfr.gov.ru/en/press_center/~2023/01/25/250437 | Child payments were standardized onto a fixed delivery date, reducing administrative friction for families. This is modest but genuine improvement in access to support. | `6B.10, 6B.5, 6B.7` |
| Pro | `More than a million families received a one-time payment at the birth of a child last year` | Social Fund of Russia | 2023-01-25 | https://sfr.gov.ru/en/press_center/~2023/01/25/250435 | The birth allowance was presented as due regardless of income or employment status, which is a rule-based benefit rather than a loyalty reward. That helps ordinary families at the margin. | `6B.10, 6B.5, 6B.7` |
| Pro | `Russian Government says almost 3,000 school buses were delivered and primary pupils got free hot meals` | Government of the Russian Federation | 2024 retrospective on 2023 | https://government.ru/en/news/51246/ | The government reported school buses, free hot meals for all primary pupils, and higher pay for teachers and educational advisers. If accurate, these are concrete child-welfare and access gains, though the source is retrospective and official. | `6B.10, 6B.2, 6B.7` |
| Pro | `Rosstat lowered 2023 poverty to 9.3%` | Rosstat | 2024-03-06 | https://www.rosstat.gov.ru/folder/313/document/232165 | Official statistics say poverty fell in 2023 and attribute part of the decline to targeted social programs, rising real wages, and pensions. This is the strongest aggregate pro-side evidence, though it still does not prove broad life chances improved evenly. | `6B.10, 6B.2, 6B.5` |
| Con | `In wartime Russia, soaring prices bite as election looms` | Reuters | 2023-11-16 | https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/in-wartime-russia-soaring-prices-bite-as-election-looms-3235923 | Reuters reported families cutting back because baby food, nappies, and other essentials became much more expensive. This directly reduced day-to-day life chances for households with children. | `6B.10, 6B.6` |
| Con | `Russian inflation accelerates in November, rate hike beckons` | Reuters | 2023-12-08 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy/russian-inflation-accelerates-in-november-rate-hike-becks-3252956 | Inflation accelerated, households had limited savings, and living standards were dragged down. That is direct counterevidence to a claim that 2023 left ordinary people materially better off. | `6B.10, 6B.6` |
| Con | `Everything for the front: Russia allots a third of 2024 spending to defence` | Reuters | 2023-09-29 | https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russias-2024-defense-spending-rise-record-share-budget-2023-09-29/ | Defence spending was set to take about a third of the budget, showing that war priorities crowded out civilian investment. That weakens long-run opportunities in health, education, and mobility. | `6B.10, 6B.2, 6B.9` |
| Con | `The rise and stagnation of Russia's economy during Putin's tenure` | Reuters | 2023-12-08 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy/the-rise-and-stagnation-of-russias-economy-during-putins-tenure-3252925 | Reuters’ long-run assessment says Russia moved from early gains to stagnation, with health and education spending barely rising in real terms for over a decade. That is strong context against a claim of durable improvement in ordinary people’s future prospects. | `6B.10, 6B.2, 6B.9` |
| Con | `Freedom in the World 2023: Russia` | Freedom House | 2023 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2023 | Freedom House says schooling was subordinated to patriotic education, dissenting educators were punished, and corruption was pervasive. That means social institutions were not mainly building broad life chances. | `6B.10, 6B.8, 6B.9` |

Search gap: I found some real 2023 improvements in universal benefits and official poverty metrics, but little evidence that they translated into durable, broad-based upward mobility. The main constraint remains the war economy: prices rose, defence consumed a much larger share of the budget, and institutions stayed personalist and politicized.
